Which Readings a Chart's Coordinate Enters

Source: R/inference.R
jacobian_depends.Rd

Reads a readable block's Jacobian as a statement about dependence: TRUE where a quantity depends on a coordinate, FALSE where the entry is the floating-point image of a structural zero.

Usage

jacobian_depends(J)

Arguments

J

The Jacobian of a readable block, quantities by coordinates.

Value

A logical matrix of the same shape, TRUE where the quantity in that row depends on the coordinate in that column. A row that is zero throughout depends on nothing and comes back all FALSE.

Details

The reading replaces the test == 0, an exact comparison on a quantity that the chart produces by arithmetic. On a covariance that a class carries, whose chart is parameters7::dr_prod(2), a standard deviation is a function of its own log coordinate only, so its entry in the correlation column is structurally zero. The entry that is computed can be a small nonzero number from cancellation, and an exact comparison then reads it as a dependence, which removes the standard error and the interval of the standard deviation for a dependence that does not exist.

A Jacobian entry is judged against the largest entry of its own row, because a row is a gradient, and the tolerance is sqrt(.Machine$double.eps), the point beyond which a differentiated quantity cannot be distinguished from the rounding of the quantities from which it was formed. The two possible errors are asymmetric, so the tolerance errs on the generous side: a genuine dependence of relative size below sqrt(eps) that is read as zero changes a variance contribution by a relative amount of order 1e-16, whereas a cancellation artifact read as a dependence removes the standard error of a quantity.

See also

readable_hyper_rows(), summary_blocks()
